narrative:
The model estimates a 61% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward you staying. Most employees the model expects to remain with the company also fall into this early-career group, so the system sees your limited tenure as a stabilizing factor rather than a risk.

However, two other aspects pushed the prediction in the opposite direction, toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here had a notable impact, suggesting external opportunities may tempt you away. Additionally, the length of time you have spent in your current role (also 1-5 years) contributed further toward the decision to leave, as it indicates you are still building roots in this specific organization.

Taken together, these elements created enough concern about potential turnover that the system could not confidently support a promotion at this time.

Your organization should discuss ways to strengthen your sense of belonging and explore how to match or exceed the external opportunities you are receiving. You may wish to reflect on what would make staying long-term more appealing. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook for future opportunities. (218 words)
